'''''Opuntia robusta''''', the '''wheel cactus''', '''nopal tapon''', or '''camuesa''',  is a species of [[cactus]] in the family [[Cactaceae]].<ref name=APNI/> It is native and [[endemism|endemic]] to central and northern [[Mexico]] to within {{convert|100|miles}} of the [[Arizona]] and [[New Mexico]] borders where it grow from {{convert|5,000|to|10,000|ft}} on rocky slopes, open shrub lands, woodlands and mixed with other cactus and succulents.

==Description==
{{One source|section
| date = June 2021
}}Plants are commonly around {{convert|1|m|in|abbr=on|sigfig=1}} high, though they may grow to over {{convert|3|m|ft|abbr=on|sigfig=1|}} high when supported.<ref name=Parsons>{{cite book|author=Parsons, W.T.| title=Noxious Weeds of Victoria| publisher=Inkata Press|location= Australia | year=1981 | isbn=0909605009}}</ref>

The flattened stem segments are fleshy, round and blue-grey in colour.<ref name=Parsons/> These are up to {{convert|30|cm|ft|abbr=on|sigfig=1}} in diameter and have the length of sharp spines up to {{convert|5|cm|in|abbr=on|sigfig=1}}.<ref name=Parsons/> Yellow, sessile flowers with a fleshy base are produced on the edges of the upper stem segments.<ref name=Parsons/> These are followed by barrel-shaped fleshy fruits which are pink or purple and up to {{convert|8|cm|in|abbr=on|sigfig=1}} long.<ref name=Parsons/>

''Opuntia robusta'' has populations that are [[dioecious]], hermaphrodite, or trioecious (containing male, female, and hermaphrodite individuals).<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.3732/ajb.0800301|title=Reproductive implications of combined and separate sexes in a trioecious population of Opuntia robusta (Cactaceae)|year=2009|last1=Del Castillo|first1=R. F.|last2=Argueta|first2=S. T.|journal=American Journal of Botany|volume=96|issue=6|pages=1148–1158|pmid=21628265}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The species was first formally described in 1837 in ''Enumeratio Diagnostica Cactearum hucusque Cognitarum''.<ref name=APNI/> It has naturalised in the states of [[South Australia]], [[New South Wales]], [[Queensland]] and [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] in [[Australia]].<ref name=APNI/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Opuntia~robusta|title = PlantNET - FloraOnline}}</ref>
